title: Who's Buying, Who's Selling? Understanding FPI and DII in Our Markets
description: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) and Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) are major players in the Indian stock market. FPIs are overseas funds investing.

faq.q: What factors influence FPIs to buy or sell?
faq.a: FPI decisions are influenced by many factors including global interest rates (especially US Fed rates), crude oil prices, geopolitical events, the strength of the US dollar, and India's economic growth prospects and corporate earnings.

faq.q: How can I track FPI and DII activity?
faq.a: Most financial news websites and stock market portals publish daily or monthly data on FPI and DII buying/selling activity. You can also find provisional data on the NSE and BSE websites.

faq.q: Do FPIs and DIIs invest in all types of stocks?
faq.a: Generally, FPIs tend to focus more on large-cap stocks, while DIIs often show interest across large, mid, and small-cap segments, depending on their fund mandates and market outlook.

faq.q: Does FPI selling always mean the market will crash?
faq.a: Not necessarily. While significant FPI selling can put downward pressure on the market, strong buying by DIIs can often cushion the fall. The market's direction depends on a combination of factors, not just FPI activity.
Yes, FPIs are regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). They need to register with SEBI and comply with various rules regarding their investments and disclosures.
